quest.title: For Our Saurian Companion
quest.description: Since you've got a free moment, why not take a walk around the Children of Echoes?
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x3

chapter.num: Tournament of Glory in Bloom: Act I
chapter.title: For Our Saurian Companion

talks.objective: Go to the Children of Echoes

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why are all these people gathered around? Did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: How's it looking, doc? Is there... any hope for him?
Chill, bro. I'm thinking.
This dude's... Milray, right? What a lil' champ... Barely made a noise, despite all the pain he must be in. Did he fight in the war?

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: That's right. We'd never normally send such a young Tepetlisaur into battle, but we couldn't stop him. Developed a real knack for sneaking past us and running off to the frontline to fight the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: He's a smart one, that's for sure. Might not be the strongest, but he ran rings around those Abyssal monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: We even awarded him a Warrior's Medal after the war ended. But then he took a turn for the worse a few days ago. He's been having fainting spells ever since...
Poor little guy... Already a battle-worn veteran, yet still so young.

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: *whimper*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Kachina, what's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, long time no see.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: So basically, there's this young Tepetlisaur in our tribe called Milray. We're not sure what's wrong with him, but he's been getting weaker and weaker by the day. Ifa's taking a look at him.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Naiyan, who he grew up with, is here too. We're all really worried about him.

dialogues.speaker: Tiyaca
dialogues.text: When my daughter got lost in the mountains, it was Milray who helped bring her back.

dialogues.speaker: Yolehua
dialogues.text: To think that he made it through the war, but now that peace has finally come... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Steady there, bro. We'll find a way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And you are...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, you're that... Qucu-Thesaurus from the vet clinic!

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Huh? What are you on about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this "Ifa" you just mentioned is actually—

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Hey, yo, everyone, please chill! I think I've got this figured out.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: For a juvenile saurian, he showed remarkable courage in the war, but he's too young to be using that much phlogiston.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: As a result, he developed a rare pathological change. The initial symptoms might not have been obvious, but he's gone untreated for so long that his condition is now very serious.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: You mean he originally got sick during the war, but the symptoms only just started to show up now?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: That's right. He may have just been acting tough this whole time... Didn't want his friends stressing out over him.

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Wooo... Rrrooo!

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Rroooh...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Ifa, there must be something you can do, right? Please, help him!

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Something this rare? I don't have anything on hand that can treat it.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Good news is that I read about a similar case back when I was still studying. The scroll mentioned two essential ingredients.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: First up, an herbaceous perennial known as an "Ocean Zephyr"... Though they can grow practically anywhere, they're exceedingly rare.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: The second... Honestly, I couldn't figure it out back then either. The name recorded was "Sacred Flame Crystal," but there wasn't much else to go on beyond that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sacred Flame... Like the one burning in the Stadium?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: When Mualani and I took part in the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, we collected loads of Contending Sparks during the team stage.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Apparently they're sparks from the Sacred Flame itself. They even make you feel all warm and fuzzy while you carry them! Do you think these Crystals might be something similar?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: From the name, I'd say we're lookin' for a rarer, purer form of Sacred Flame.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sure there's even such a thing? We've been in Natlan for ages now, but we've never come across anything like that.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: ...So it would seem, as it happens.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina & Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: For real, Uncle Pacal?

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: It's a coincidence that I've even heard of it. Apparently, the people of Natlan knew how to make a special kind of "Sacred Flame Crystal" way back when.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: I'm not sure exactly how they did it, but the other chiefs might know something... I'll go ask them.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Thank you, Ifa, your diagnosis was a huge help. Mind if I keep you a little longer?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Sure thing, dude. I'll stick around until we've got some results.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Great. In that case, let's go our separate ways for now. Milray needs some proper rest, and he's not gonna get that with so many people gathered around.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: I'll let you all know as soon as there's any news. Fingers crossed, he'll soon be on the mend.

talks.objective: Chat with Ifa

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: What up, my dudes?

choices.text: Umm... Hello?

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Haha, hey, come on, chill.

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: The name's Ifa, a vet from the Flower-Feather Clan. This here's my assistant, Cacucu. Dude's all about copying what others say.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're...

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon, yeah? Everyone's heard all about you two — you're absolute legends!

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: The total package: Brave, wise, and strong... Best hero duo I've ever seen, no contest!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, hehe, you're making Paimon blush!

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Truth is, I spent the war treating wounded saurians. Never got a chance to fight alongside you.

choices.text: You saved so many saurian lives. That was an amazing contribution too!

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Yo, thanks bro! I appreciate that!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: There was always a long line outside Ifa's clinic back then. Even Cacucu was so busy he was running around like a headless chicken.

response.speaker: Cacucu
response.text: Seriously! Seriously!

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: True that... more wounded were pilin' up by the day.

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Dude, the Abyss is no joke, sneaky enough to hit us right where it hurts. Lots of docs have dropped at their posts over the last few years...

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: There's some fresh talent rolling in recently, I'm hoping they can step up quick. But vet med's no joke. There's a ton of challenges to overcome before you can be a qualified vet.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's rough...

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: No matter how hard you hit the books, you're still gonna run into all kinds of weird diseases that are hard to treat. Like Milray's — so rare it doesn't even have a name.

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: If my old man hadn't forced me to read all kinds of different stuff when I was a kid, I'd probably only be able to suggest a more conservative treatment. It's true what they say, bro — there's always more to learn.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so your dad was a vet too?

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Yeah, totally. Our family's medical knowledge has been passed down over generations. My old man started steering me toward being a vet when I was a kid, schooling me on all kinds of herbs. And man, if I forgot anything, out came the broom.

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: My family's been vets for generations now. No clue who it was that kicked off the tradition though, you know?

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Back when I was a kid, my dad said something about our skills being "medicine born of guilt"... But the reason we got into it doesn't really matter — what matters is that it's useful.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guilt? Sounds pretty strange to Paimon. Usually, you only feel guilty when you've done something wrong...

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Who knows? After he passed, there wasn't anybody else I could ask. I figure it's because guilt gnaws at anyone practicing medicine. When you fail to fix someone up... I've been there.

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: So I'm gonna do my best to make sure that doesn't happen this time. I don't recall ever seeing a record of any patient with his malady who was successfully cured, so maybe Milray will be the first.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You've got this, bro.

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Heck yeah, I do.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You talk for a while longer...

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Oh? Looks like the chiefs are back. Let's go see what they have to say.

choices.text: A legend among vets.
Your rep precedes you, bro. Respect.

response.speaker: Ifa
response.text: Man, I can tell we're totally on the same wavelength.

talks.objective: Ask the tribal chiefs about the situation

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: The last time I was here, I remember seeing him happily rolling around with Ayo. This is so sudden...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Well, as the saying goes, "illness strikes like a landslide." It's not uncommon for people and saurians to just collapse overnight.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Given that he first fell sick during the war, he's done well to make it this far.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Hey, little guy, are you okay? Does it hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: For one so young to risk life and limb on the field of battle... This, too, is a responsibility we adults must bear.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, all six tribal chiefs in one place! Not something you see every day...

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Haha, it's true that we used to hardly ever meet up like this. The affairs of our own tribes were usually enough to keep us all swamped.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: These days, though, group dinners on our days off have practically become the routine, so don't look too surprised.

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: Group dinners? More like group mooching! You guys always seem to end up at my place... So shameless.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Well, your cooking is too good to resist. You've seen how hopeless the rest of us are in that regard... *ahem* Anyway, let's get down to business.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Ifa, we've been informed about the situation. Once again, it's a good thing you were here to help out.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Milray and the other Tepetlisaurs have helped transport goods for the Flower-Feather Clan in the past. We won't just stand by and watch while he suffers.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: I just happened to come across a record of a case like his back home, but I don't know anything about this "Sacred Flame Crystal."

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: I haven't heard of it either. Can the Sacred Flame even take other forms?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: It can indeed. While I've never seen this happen in the flesh, I have read references to it in woven scrolls.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: In ancient Natlan, besides the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, there is said to have been another way to produce Sacred Flame, known as the "Bloomflower Trials."

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: It was a combat exercise held jointly by the six tribes that was even more intense than the Pilgrimage, so they occasionally yielded an even purer form of Sacred Flame.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina & Paimon
dialogues.text: Sacred Flame Crystals!?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: For real? How have I never heard of that...?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Simple. The Bloomflower Trials haven't been held for centuries.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there some hidden story behind this?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Something seems to have happened the last time they were held, but it was so long ago that I don't know the specifics.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: The more reasonable explanation is this — that people once believed these Sacred Flame Crystals to be vessels of extraordinary power, and that warriors could use them to enhance their own strength.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: In reality, they turned out to be far less miraculous than hoped for. In some rare, very specific circumstances, they proved irreplaceable, but they were not so different from the regular Sacred Flame in essence.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: The Pilgrimage produced enough Sacred Flame, making the Bloomflower Trials obsolete. And thus, they were forgotten.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Ah, I get it. So to save Milray, we have to revive the Bloomflower Trials and get all six tribes to take part. That sounds rough...

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: I'd say we'd be better off not treating it like some kind of hassle.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: All six tribes need to take part, sure, but not everyone has to show up. We can keep it voluntary, so warriors who happen to have time can sign up and fight it out of their own accord.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Since the war ended, the Pilgrimage has become more like a tournament for our warriors to compete in and keep themselves in shape, so why not let them hone their skills on a fresh new stage?

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: We should never drop our guard completely, even in times of peace. Put like that, it seems high time we restarted the Bloomflower Trials.

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: I'm with you on that. Nothing gets the blood pumping like a contest to see which tribe's the strongest, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: No objections on my part.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: I'll go discuss this with the others. I'm sure there'll be plenty of warriors who'll be itching to take part.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: I can't speak for everyone else, but I can guarantee that Mualani will be there — there's nothing she loves more than a lively occasion.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: And I guess your vote was a foregone conclusion, eh, Pacal? Great, we're all in agreement, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice!

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: ...Thanks, everyone, it really means a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Let's head back to our tribes and see how many people are willing to sign up. If interest is high, we'll hold a big event, but if not, we'll keep it small.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Agreed. Rules will be crucial too. A competition without rules is just mindless violence, and that's not what we want.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I'll draw up an outline. Let's meet up at the Speaker's Chamber later — after all, we'll still need the Pyro Archon's final approval.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, and we'll also need some Ocean Zephyrs to cure Milray. Who'll go gather them while we're organizing the Trials?

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: I've got that covered... I just noticed that some of Milray's friends have shown up.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: You mean these saurians? You're right, there's all sorts. Seems like he's quite the popular little fella, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Cacucu, can you hit them up and ask if they'd be down to lend a claw?

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Sure thing, bro. I've got you, bro.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Hah, must be nice having a saurian companion who can talk...

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: Well, if that's everything, how about we call it a day?

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Alright. See you later.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Ifa, let's head back — and bring these saurians along too. We've gotta teach them how to identify Ocean Zephyrs.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Seeya, little guy. We'll come visit you again soon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, they sure are quick on their feet!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess they're chiefs for a reason — when they decide on something, it gets done right away...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: More the "Let's sleep on it" type, are we, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, but that's what you're here for, right? Whenever Paimon puts things off, even for just a while, you'll handle them straight away!

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: Oh wow... No way, bro!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Even Cacucu's done with this conversation...

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: I'll go spread the word. Kachina, you gonna sign up?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: O—Of course!

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: #In that case, let's head over together. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, see you at the Speaker's Chamber in a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: See ya!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So far, so good! At this rate, Milray will be better in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: *whimper*...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, you're awake? Wanna try getting a bit more sleep?

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Rrrrawrrr...

choices.text: I feel like...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You think so? Is he feeling hungry, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Cacucu! Can you help us transl—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, long gone! Oh no, he does seem pretty anxious... What are you trying to say, little guy?

choices.text: ...He has something to say?

talks.objective: Indwell a Tepetlisaurus, then talk to the little saurian

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: *Rrraw* *cough* *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Everything okay, Milray? Do you wanna eat something?

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Wh—Why don't I go pick you some fruit?

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Thanks for looking after me, Naiyan. I'll be fine...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello, Milray and Naiyan.

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Oh? Who are you...?

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Haven't seen you around here before, hmm... Have you come to visit Milray, too?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah! I just wanted to tell you that you have nothing to worry about, okay? Those nice humans have found a way to cure you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It won't be long before they've gathered enough Ocean Zephyrs and Sacred Flame Crystals, so hang in there — you'll be on the mend soon.

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Sacred Flame Crystals... *cough* *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: Milray...

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: That's exactly what I'm worried about. Those nice humans have no idea how dangerous Sacred Flame Crystals are...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Dangerous?

dialogues.speaker: Milray
dialogues.text: Yes, very dangerous. They can beguile human hearts, turn friends into enemies... The humans must be very careful...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Milray struggles to say something else, but he soon falls unconscious once more.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ("Beguile human hearts"? The chiefs didn't mention anything about that before... Could there be unknown risks associated with using Sacred Flame Crystals?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But, more importantly... If even the chiefs know nothing about this, despite all the knowledge they possess, then where did Milray and Naiyan come to hear of it?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Naiyan, who told you guys that Sacred Flame Crystals were dangerous?

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: A mysterious Qucusaur we met while fighting those big monsters... He was the one who told us.

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: I still remember how our friends were all running around in a panic the first time Milray passed out...
Not this disease, not again... We'll need to find Ocean Zephyrs and Sacred Flame Crystals...
But Sacred Flame Crystals can beguile human hearts, turn friends into enemies... What should I do?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where did this Qucusaur find out, then?

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: I don't know... He often said things we couldn't understand. Apart from us, no other little saurians wanted to play with him, and as far as I could tell, he didn't have any human companions either.

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: But I'm sure he wouldn't have lied to us. He's saved us many times, and we're very close friends.

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: I really, really hope that Milray recovers soon. But if Sacred Flame Crystals genuinely are that dangerous... I don't think that's the way he would want to be saved.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm here to help.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll remind the humans to be careful. In the meantime, you take good care of Milray, alright? Just make sure he doesn't worry too much and gets lots of rest.

dialogues.speaker: Naiyan
dialogues.text: You'd do that for him? Thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is becoming more mysterious by the minute. With Mavuika and the six chiefs present, I'm sure everything will be alright — but still, I'd better find a chance to talk to Mavuika about it.)

talks.objective: Go to the Speaker's Chamber to meet Mavuika

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I've read through your proposal, and it sounds like a great idea.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Even if it wasn't for Milray's situation, there'd be many reasons to start holding the Bloomflower Trials again. How many warriors have been signing up?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Far more than we anticipated.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Our warriors sure are fired up! The ones who came late even held a protest outside the signup booth, so we had to make an exception by adding a few more spots.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: So many people have signed up that we've had to divide the competition up into main matches and exhibition matches. Each main match will pit two different tribes against one another, while the exhibition matches will see three tribes going up against another three.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I'm planning to limit the number of spots for the exhibition matches. Accidents are more likely in tangled melees, so with fewer contestants, we can ensure that any injuries will be attended to promptly.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Well, you've clearly thought this through with care. You have my approval — and don't worry, I'll find a way to fund it.

dialogues.speaker: Chiefs
dialogues.text: Thank you, Archon!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Where will the Trials be held? I'll stop by later to see how things are going, but I won't be taking part. Wouldn't want to spoil everyone else's fun.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: The main venue will be near the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, with additional arenas set up around the various tribes.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Alright, I'm all out of questions. Keep at it, everyone, and thanks for your hard work.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: In that case, we'll be off. It's time we started organizing crews to set up the venues.

dialogues.speaker: Acatl
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... Good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Good luck with... what, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hey! It's been a while, you two. Are you here about the Bloomflower Trials too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, we sure are. Sounds like everything's going to plan!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "Bloomflower Trials"... The name alone fills me with nostalgia. I first heard about it from my dad, who first heard about it from his dad, my old grandpa.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess that means they were last held at least 500 years ago...? Wait a sec, no, it must have been much earlier than that, then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, when you put it like that, it does feel kinda surreal that we're doing something that hasn't been done in such a long time!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: True, but I've got a good feeling about this. We'll pull it off, rest assured.

choices.text: Do you know anything about Sacred Flame Crystals?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Hmm? What makes you ask?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We've heard rumors that Sacred Flame Crystals can "beguile human hearts"...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Hmm... I've never heard such a rumor before. And rationally speaking, it just doesn't even seem possible.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The rules governing the Ode of Resurrection have protected Natlan for many long years, and these rules are themselves fueled by the Sacred Flame's power. We've been working with the Sacred Flame all this time, and we've never noticed anything unusual about it.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: In essence, Sacred Flame Crystals are just another form of the Sacred Flame. I can't imagine how they could possibly "beguile human hearts."

choices.text: That's very true.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: So please, be at ease. And besides, even if they did harbor some kind of evil power, it will not cause any real trouble in the Natlan we now live in — not if I have anything to say about it.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Our main priority right now is to hold the Bloomflower Trials so we can collect enough Sacred Flame Crystals to heal that little Tepetlisaurus.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, it's so reassuring to have you on our side, Mavuika.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Well, there are some things even I can't handle.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: For example... It just came to my attention that you've got some people waiting for you outside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Who could they be?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: You'll find out soon enough... Go on, now. Don't keep them waiting.

choices.text: I find it hard to imagine too.
Is there anything dangerous about them?

talks.objective: Leave the Speaker's Chamber

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Finally, you're here!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon. So basically...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hold up, what happened to "first come, first served"? What I'm saying is, I get to go first!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, what's going on? Why has everyone turned up all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Umm, so...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: *ahem* So, you know about the Bloomflower Trials, right? I— I mean we, were wondering... Have you decided which tribe you'll join? If not, how about the People of the Springs?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhhh, what—!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're allowed to take part too!?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Given that the Trials haven't been held in so long, we're creating a new set of rules for them, separate from the ones for the Pilgrimage.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: All of the chiefs have agreed. But whether or not you compete, or which tribe you support... Well, that's completely up to you.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: As the hero who saved Natlan, your participation would be a huge morale boost for whoever you choose to join. In other words, recruiting you is every tribe's top priority right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so that's what's going on! No wonder Chief Acatl wished us good luck just now... He must have known this was coming!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hehe — and that's all for the chit-chat. I hope you're ready for some serious incentives.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: How do you like the sound of luxury hot spring vouchers? I'll even throw in a selection of fine gifts from the shop!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Luxury hot springs... Sounds like Paimon's perfect vacation!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: If you join the Scions of the Canopy, we'll hold a great barbecue in your honor. The finest quality meat, all you can eat.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: And if you join right away, you'll even stand a chance of being taken on as a sidekick of the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yeah, no one wants that.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Kinich, you little—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All you can eat barbecue... *salivating*...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Join up with the Collective of Plenty, and I'll provide a year's worth of training sessions and a personalized nutrition plan to help you become stronger than you already are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm... Paimon's not too keen on training, but getting stronger does sound tempting...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: All I've got to offer are freshly picked vegetables. But I can guarantee they are really tasty.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooohh, could Paimon get some samples?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Fancy some flying lessons? Or you could just hitch a ride. I'll take you soaring through the skies myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Flying's kinda what Paimon does for a living, but flying around with {NICKNAME} sounds like it could be a lot of fun too!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I—I can bake Saurus Crackers and Grainfruit Chips!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, Paimon loves those too... This is such a tough choice.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not just 'cause the freebies are tempting, but also because picking one tribe feels like we're betraying all the others...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know what? Paimon's decided... to leave this one to you.

choices.text: How about I join you all, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh, Paimon's pretty sure that isn't an option...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Actually, it's not a bad idea... It could work for the exhibition matches, at least.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: There'd be three tribes on one side versus three on the other for those. So, first half, you're on our side. Second half, on theirs. Sounds fair enough, right?

response.speaker: Ororon
response.text: Huh, I hadn't thought of that... Pretty clever.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What, really? Then as for those perks you mentioned earlier... Hehe...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Don't worry, my offer still stands. Enjoying ourselves is the number one priority here!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: So it's settled, then? For the first half of the exhibition match, you'll fight alongside us Scions of the Canopy, People of the Springs, and the Children of Echoes against the other three tribes.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Haha, feels just like the old days when we used to fight side by side. We're gonna be unstoppable!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Alright, it's nearly time. Let's get ready and head over there together.

choices.text: "Tumaini" belongs to all of Natlan, after all.

talks.objective: Participate in the first half of the exhibition match
Discuss your battle plan

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, so this is our base. According to the rules, all we have to do is capture three of their bases in a row, and we win!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go over our game plan.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Hehe, the Almighty Dragonlord K'uhul Ajaw needs only lift a claw, and... Poof! All that you behold shall be turned to ashes!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Mess up our match, and I'll lock you up till it's all over.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: *grumble*... You killjoy!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hehe, we're a real dream team! Let's just charge right in!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: We know each other pretty well, so working together should be a breeze. Still, let's not get careless.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: There are a lot of cliffs nearby, so our vision will be obscured. They could ambush us from the high ground too.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: In that case, let's follow the water instead!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: See that flag over there — that's the Collective of Plenty's base, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We'll approach swiftly on the water, sweep in and capture the base, then move up to the high ground!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I like the way you think.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I trust your judgment too, Mualani.

choices.text: They won't know what hit 'em.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Alright then! Time for me and my Sharky Surfboard to strut our stuff!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I'll take point! Everyone, follow me!

choices.text: We'll catch them completely off guard.

talks.objective: Attack the Collective of Plenty's base

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Here by the water route, just as expected... Classic People of the Springs thinking.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Huh...? They saw through our plan?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: No choice but to face them head on now.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I'm ready!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Alright then, time for a real showdown!

talks.objective: Defeat the base guards and switch the flag
Attack the Masters of the Night-Wind's base

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #You're finally here, {M#Gramps}{F#other Granny}.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: If I'm back home too late, my vegetables will get thirsty...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we'll make this quick for ya!

talks.objective: Defeat the base guards and switch the flag
Discuss your next move

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Alright, we've taken the Masters of the Night-Wind's base too.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Look, up there on the mountain — the flag of the Flower-Feather Clan!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, looks like they're already on high alert.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yeah. Not only do they have the high ground, but they're highly mobile, too. With our current forces, a frontal assault won't be easy.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Looks like I showed up right on cue, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay, you're here too, Xilonen!

choices.text: They did mention reinforcements...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Let's save the small talk for when the flag's in the bag.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Now that backup's arrived, let's split up into two teams.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I'll lead a frontal assault to draw their fire.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The rest of you find another route up and strike directly at the heart of their base.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hehe, I can taste our victory already!

choices.text: ...But this is a formidable ally indeed.

talks.objective: Launch a surprise attack on the Flower-Feather Clan's base from behind

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Well, would you look at that. You managed to find a gap in our defenses somehow.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But this is just the beginning, so stay on your feet... if you can.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: We're not gonna lose!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Well said. Let's do this.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Let's have ourselves some fun!

talks.objective: Defeat the base guards and switch the flag
Conduct a post-battle review

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Phew... Does that mean we've won?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hehe, told you we'd be unstoppable!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Well that was pretty exhilarating, even as battles go.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You can say that again! I was still fighting off Qucusaur Riders halfway up the mountainside when I heard you'd already taken the base.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: That was well played!

choices.text: Thanks for covering us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, the going would've been way tougher if we had fought our way up...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: How about the Sacred Flame Crystals? Did anyone manage to get their hands on some?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I found a few shards, but they were only about as big as Grainfruit Chips. I gave them to the marshals from the Masters of the Night-Wind on our way back.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Yes, and they gave them to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Granny Citlali! Are you here to take part in the Bloomflower Trials too?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I devised the techniques for the main matches, so of course I would show up.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Those marshals handed the Sacred Flame Crystals over as soon as they saw me.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I did a quick tally. At this rate, we should have enough by the event's end.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: That's awesome!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Even Citlali didn't notice anything strange about the Sacred Flame Crystals. Am I just overthinking this?)

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Well, since everything's gone so smoothly, why don't we hit the hot springs tonight?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I'm all for it. There's nothing like letting our hair down after a hard day's work. And good food and drink wouldn't go down badly either.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: How about we head over there together? You can all hitch a ride on Turbo Twirly!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Sorry, but I need to head back to the workshop to finish up some forging commissions first. Let's meet at the People of the Springs later this evening.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I need to help at the shop anyway, so I'll pick up some snacks there. See you all tonight!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I might be a bit late. If you're all there earlier, feel free to start without me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! Paimon can't wait!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: ...Sure!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: In that case, I guess I'll be off too. See you tonight!

choices.text: ...We wouldn't have taken the base the way we did otherwise.

talks.objective: Head to the hot springs and wait for the evening party
Take part in the hot springs party

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hurry up, guys! You're the last ones left!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Come on, I'll take you to get changed.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You remember where the changing rooms are, right? I'm pretty sure I showed you last time.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Time sure flies... Ahh, sorry, let's save the reminiscing for later! Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You get changed in a familiar spot...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Woohoo! Let's get this party started!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Ah, this is the life! Hear this, hot spring, I hereby bestow upon you the name of the Almighty Dragonlord!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All the fatigue just floats away... If only we could do this every day!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Aren't you gonna join us, Xilonen?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I'm not a huge fan of being in the water. This right here's more my kind of spot.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: ...And last, but not least: "Surf, Turf, and Perch."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! That smells amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold your horses! There's a time for fun and games, and it's not when there's delicious food already on the table... Wait for Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Mwahaha, take that, Kinich! Bow before my greatness!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hey, watch it Ajaw! You're splashing water everywhere!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Whew...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #This is so tasty! {NICKNAME}, you've gotta try it!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Kachina... Teyvat to Kachina! I made Saurus Crackers, come have some!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Ahh... O—Okay! I'll be right there!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Kinich, you churlish— Unhand me! Let me go!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a lively end to a fun-filled gathering, everyone heads their separate ways...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Whew, thanks for sticking around to help me clean up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problem at all, we had a blast!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Parties are always extra lively when you guys are here! It was so much fun.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: By the way, I couldn't help feeling that there was something on Kachina's mind during dinner...

choices.text: I noticed that too.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hmm, it's strange... She usually comes to me for advice when something's bothering her.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Maybe this is something... different? Sorry to do this, but could you try asking her?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! We'll ask the next time we're alone with her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If there was something we could do to help, there's no way we'd stand by!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Thanks, that makes me feel a lot better!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Anyway, I'll be heading off now too. Just remember, you'll always be welcome to come hang out with me at the People of the Springs!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bye for now, see you soon!

choices.text: She's been a bit off since the exhibition match ended...

talks.objective: Additional
Additional

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: A new competition brings a new challenge... And who knows? Maybe even a whole new story.

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (It seems like the Bloomflower Trials are all set to take place, which means we've got the Sacred Flame Crystals covered, and Milray's saurian buddies are out collecting Ocean Zephyrs too. So, on paper at least, everything should be fine...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (But why does Milray look so anxious? Has his condition gotten worse? We'd better ask him, just in case.)
